extracted.intended_audience: science journalists and public information officers (PIOs) at federal agencies (and journalists covering government-funded science)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines defining principles and practical standards to govern interactions, access, and communications between science journalists and public information officers (and other sources) at federal science agencies. Covers agency responsibilities, journalist obligations, and expectations for the journalist–PIO relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalist: Anyone engaged in the editorially independent reporting of news or information for the public. Public information officer (PIO): Anyone employed by an agency for the purposes of disseminating information to the public or facilitating interactions between agency employees and journalists. Source: Anyone whose comment is sought by a journalist for the purposes of reporting news or information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes who the standards apply to and clarifies role boundaries for subsequent standards and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle — Truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Science is a powerful mechanism for pursuing truth and producing knowledge. The public is entitled to scientific information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames the purpose of access and communication: enabling truth-seeking and public entitlement to scientific information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle — Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific information is valuable to the extent that it is conveyed accurately, with appropriate context, and without hype, exaggeration, slant, or omission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to journalists and PIOs; underpins obligations to correct errors and avoid misleading presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle — Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: The public has a right to know what is happening inside taxpayer-funded agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports obligations on agencies to publish policies, contact information, and to facilitate open access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle — Accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: The public requires access to information to evaluate the actions and decisions of public agencies and officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justifies open access and the need for agencies to avoid restricting information flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle — Openness
rubrics_metrics.description: Granting full and equal access to all journalists best promotes the public's ability to know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourages exclusive access arrangements and supports fair treatment of outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle — Respect
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists and PIOs deserve respect, in recognition of the fact that both play valuable roles in communicating scientific information to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports civil, professional interactions and mutual recognition of roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of journalists in society
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists are a crucial independent source of information about the government, including science produced, funded, or used by government entities. Dynamic and unrestricted reporting is fundamental to allowing journalists to produce the most informative and comprehensive stories possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains why journalists' access and independence are important public goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of PIOs in society
rubrics_metrics.description: PIOs play important roles in facilitating journalists' access to government sources, and in providing critical information to journalists and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges PIO contribution and the need for workable collaboration between journalists and PIOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public service obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists and PIOs work on behalf of the public, not just the institutions that employ them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames both parties' responsibilities as serving the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalists' direct, unrestricted access to federal sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should have direct, unrestricted access to sources in the federal government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core standard: agencies and PIOs should not unreasonably block or funnel journalist access to scientists or other sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: PIOs should encourage direct communication
rubrics_metrics.description: PIOs and federal agencies should encourage direct and unfettered communication between journalists and scientists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIOs are expected to facilitate — not to serve as barriers — to direct exchanges between reporters and subject-matter experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source freedom to choose terms of communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources should have the freedom to choose whether to speak to the media and the terms of any communication, including whether a PIO is involved in interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects source autonomy; agencies should not coerce or unduly restrict a source's ability to speak or set terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default on-the-record terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms of the communication should be clear, with the default assumption that communications with journalists are on the record unless both parties agree otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires clarity about whether an interview or comment is on the record, off the record, background, etc.; default is on-record unless explicit agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair and transparent access; no exclusive access to control coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies and PIOs should provide access to journalists in ways that are fair and transparent. Agencies and PIOs should not use exclusive access as a way to control or restrict the free flow of information, or to reward or punish particular outlets or journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourages embargo-like favoritism or selective access that skews reporting; supports equitable treatment of outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies must have public, up-to-date media and scientific integrity policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies should create and follow media and scientific integrity policies that are up-to-date and in keeping with the principles outlined here. These policies should be clearly communicated to all personnel and should be made publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency policies should be accessible online and communicated internally so employees and journalists understand expectations and protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection for scientists speaking personally
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies should clearly inform scientists and other employees that they have a right to express their personal opinions, including to the media, without fear of retribution or punishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should make clear staff rights and protect employees from retaliation for personal commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public listing of contacts and expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should publicly display on their websites work contact information for scientists, PIOs and other employees. When possible, agencies should additionally publicly display information about employee expertise and organizational charts, so that journalists can understand roles and chains of command within agencies. Such information should be kept as up-to-date as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical recommendation to support journalists' ability to identify and contact appropriate sources and understand agency structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalists' obligation to ensure accuracy and fairness (no prepublication review obligation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists have an obligation to ensure accuracy and fairness, but do not have an obligation to offer sources the opportunity to review stories or quotes before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms journalist responsibility for accuracy while rejecting routine source review as a requirement; distinguishes correction obligations from prepublication approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct factual errors transparently and promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists have an obligation to transparently, prominently, and expediently correct factual errors in stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how journalists should handle mistakes — openly and quickly — to maintain accuracy and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate deadlines clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should communicate clearly with sources and PIOs about deadlines, when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical expectation to help PIOs and sources respond in time and to foster efficient exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek comment fairly and timely; especially for criticism/ allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should seek comment from sources in a fair and timely way. Seeking official comment is particularly important in cases involving criticism or allegations of wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures balance and fairness by giving subjects opportunity to respond, especially in sensitive coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make clear sources' capacity (personal vs official)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should make clear in their stories when sources have specified that they are speaking in their personal rather than their official capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps readers understand whether a comment reflects institutional positions or individual views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properly attribute sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should properly attribute their sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard journalistic practice to identify where information comes from unless anonymity is agreed upon for legitimate reasons; ties to transparency principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek and understand agency official positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should strive to seek and understand an agency's official position on a topic or issue, when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages inclusion of formal agency perspectives alongside individual scientist views for fuller context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professionalism and civility between journalists and PIOs
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists and PIOs should treat one another with professionalism and civility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutual respect helps sustain productive relationships and public-serving communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely responses between PIOs and journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: PIOs should respond promptly to journalists' inquiries. Journalists should in turn respond promptly to PIOs who are responding to a journalist-initiated request for information or an interview, or who are providing factual corrections to a published story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages reciprocity in timeliness to keep reporting accurate and efficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalists need not disclose unrelated information to PIOs
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists need not, however, provide information to PIOs that is unrelated to a particular informational or interview request (e.g. the length or scope of a story, information about other sources contacted or information gathered, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects journalistic independence and reporting methods from being compelled by agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty between PIOs and journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: PIOs should be honest toward journalists. Journalists should be honest toward PIOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic ethical expectation to avoid deception or misrepresentation in interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not misrepresent facts by commission or omission
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists and PIOs should not misrepresent facts through commission or omission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both parties must avoid deliberate misstatement and the withholding of material facts that would mislead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix — Federal agencies' media policies (resource)
rubrics_metrics.description: The document lists federal agencies' media/scientific integrity policies that were accessible online as of publication (e.g., Department of Agriculture Scientific Integrity; NOAA/NOAA policies; EPA Scientific Integrity Policy; NASA Release of Information; NRC Guidelines for Interviews with the Media; NSF Public Communications and Media Policy, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as a pointer to existing agency policies that embody or relate to these standards; not prescriptive itself but a resource to compare and consult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix — Relevant professional codes of ethics (resource)
rubrics_metrics.description: References codes of ethics as additional examples: Society of Professional Journalists Code of Ethics, Public Relations Society of America Code of Ethics, and NASW's own Code of Ethics for Science Writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested supplemental materials for ethical decision-making and standards; NASW has not formally endorsed all listed codes but provides them for reference.
